papers.title_in_file: Exponential Quantum Advantage for Pathfinding in Regular Sunflower Graphs
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 1.1 summary of main results, Section 1.2 overview; proofs not read.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that defines the regular sunflower graph and proves an exponential quantum-classical separation for pathfinding with an adjacency list oracle.

assertions.value: The authors prove that, with high probability, a regular sunflower graph of degree at least 7 is a mild expander graph, with a spectral gap of the graph Laplacian at least inverse polylogarithmic in the graph size.
quotes: We prove that, with high probability, a regular sunflower graph of degree at least 7 is a mild expander graph, that is, the spectral gap of the graph Laplacian is at least inverse polylogarithmic in the graph size.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 3.5, listed in Section 1.1, p.5

assertions.value: The authors prove that a quantum algorithm can find the s-t path for a specific pair of vertices s and t, given s but not t at the beginning, in time poly(n).
quotes: A quantum algorithm can find the s-t path for a specific pair of vertices s and t (given s but not t at the beginning) in time poly(n) (Theorem 5.4).
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 5.4, p.6

assertions.value: The authors state the separation is for the pathfinding problem with the adjacency list oracle, and that any classical algorithm takes exponential time on the regular sunflower graph.
quotes: exponential quantum-classical separation for the pathfinding problem with the adjacency list oracle
while any classical algorithm takes exponential time
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 6.3, listed in Section 1.1, p.6
assertions.reader_inference: The separation holds in the oracle (query) model only, not for an explicit instantiation.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Reservoir Computing for Realized Volatility Forecasting
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, setup of the reservoir, results discussion, Conclusions and Outlook, closing discussion.
papers.what_it_is: An empirical study that uses a 10-qubit quantum reservoir to forecast realized volatility of the S&P 500 and compares it with econometric and machine learning models.

assertions.value: The authors report that the proposed quantum reservoir approach consistently outperforms the benchmark models across various metrics.
quotes: Our results indicate that the proposed quantum reservoir approach consistently outperforms benchmark models across various metrics
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on one forecasting task.

assertions.value: The authors state they used a quantum reservoir with 10 qubits, made of input and hidden qubits, and 3 layers.
quotes: we used a quantum reservoir with 10 qubits (comprising both input and hidden qubits such that n1 + n2 = 10) and 3 layers
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors state they do not claim a definitive quantum advantage, because such a conclusion would require rigorous theoretical proof beyond the scope of the paper.
quotes: we do not claim a definitive quantum advantage, as such a conclusion would require rigorous theoretical proof beyond the scope of this paper
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the limit of its claim.

papers.title_in_file: Expressibility-Enhancing Strategies for Quantum Neural Networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Method overview, results summary, Conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A paper that proposes four strategies to improve how well quantum neural networks approximate sinusoidal-based functions and tests them numerically.

assertions.value: The authors report that state-of-the-art QNNs with strong expressive power can have poor performance in approximating even a simple sinusoidal function.
quotes: We surprisingly discover that state-of-the-art QNNs with strong expressive power can have poor performance in approximating even just a simple sinusoidal function.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from the authors' own experiments.

assertions.value: The authors report that comparative experiments validate that the four strategies significantly increase QNN performance in approximating complex multivariable functions and reduce the circuit depth and qubits required.
quotes: Our results from comparative experiments validate that the four strategies can significantly increase the QNNs' performance in approximating complex multivariable functions and reduce the quantum circuit depth and qubits required.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the embedding and the post-measurement function should leverage problem-specific knowledge.
quotes: The embedding and post-measurement function should leverage problem-specific knowledge.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim without a dedicated test in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: This reads as a scope condition on the strategies.

papers.title_in_file: Transfer learning of optimal QAOA parameters in combinatorial optimization
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, hardware results discussion, Section IV Conclusions.
papers.what_it_is: A study that reuses pre-trained QAOA parameters from one combinatorial optimization problem on other problems, on simulators and on quantum hardware and an annealer.

assertions.value: The authors report that bin packing (BPP) gives the best transferable parameters, keeping the probability of finding the optimal solution above a quadratic speedup over random guessing for problem sizes up to 42 qubits and p = 10 layers.
quotes: Among the different problems, BPP is the one that produces the best transferable parameters, maintaining the probability of finding the optimal solution above a quadratic speedup over random guessing for problem sizes up to 42 qubits and p = 10 layers.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on small instances.

assertions.value: The authors state that the improvement from self-optimization over transfer learning does not fully compensate for the resources the optimization loop needs to find the parameters.
quotes: this improvement does not fully compensate for the resources needed for the optimization loop needed to find the parameters
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical conclusion from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state they tested 3 instances of the MIS problem with 8, 14 and 18 qubits on Rigetti's Aspen-M-3, IBM's Brisbane, IonQ's Harmony and Aria.
quotes: We test 3 different instances of the MIS problem with 8, 14, and 18 qubits with the devices used being Rigetti's Aspen-M-3, IBM's Brisbane, IonQ's Harmony, and Aria.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its hardware setup, Section IV, p.8.

assertions.value: The authors state that in one hardware case there is a slight improvement in the Aspen-M-3 result compared to the Random Sampler, but not enough to conclude that partial information about the probability distribution is recoverable.
quotes: In this case, there is a slight improvement in the Aspen-M-3 result compared to the Random Sampler, but it is not significant enough to conclude that partial information about the probability distribution is recoverable.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit of its hardware result.

papers.title_in_file: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Convolutional Neural Networks for Image Classification in Multiple Color Spaces
papers.version_note: Same arXiv id 2406.02229 (v3, 8 May 2025). The file title differs from the record's earlier Lab-colour-space title; treated as the same paper in a later version.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, simulation setup, Conclusion, limitation paragraph.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of a hybrid quantum-classical CNN for image classification in RGB, Lab, YCrCb and HSV colour spaces.

assertions.value: The authors report that the HQCNN outperforms the classical CNN across all tested color spaces for the ten-class MNIST task, with a best accuracy of 94.3% in Lab compared to 92.8% in RGB for the CNN.
quotes: Experimental results demonstrate that the HQCNN outperforms the classical CNN across all tested color spaces for the ten-class MNIST task, achieving a best accuracy of 94.3% in Lab compared to 92.8% in RGB for the CNN
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors state that all quantum simulations and computations, for both the HQCNN and the classical CNN, ran on an Apple M4 CPU.
quotes: All quantum simulations and computations for both HQCNN and classical CNN models on an Apple M4 CPU.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its computing setup.

assertions.value: The authors state the study is limited by its reliance on quantum simulations rather than NISQ hardware.
quotes: the current study is limited by its reliance on quantum simulations rather than NISQ hardware
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its limit.

papers.title_in_file: Experimental semi-autonomous eigensolver using reinforcement learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, algorithm stages, experimental result sections, Conclusions.
papers.what_it_is: An experiment on IBM quantum hardware of a feedback-loop eigensolver, cast as reinforcement learning, that uses few single-shot measurements.

assertions.value: The authors report that for a single-qubit observable both eigenvectors are obtained with fidelities over 0.97 using around 200 single-shot measurements, and for two-qubit observables fidelities over 0.91 using around 1500 single-shot measurements for the four eigenvectors.
quotes: Using this algorithm, for a single-qubit observable, we obtain both eigenvectors with fidelities over 0.97 with around 200 single-shot measurements.
For two-qubits observables, we get fidelities over 0.91 with around 1500 single-shot measurements for the four eigenvectors
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one experiment on IBM hardware.
assertions.reader_inference: The Conclusions state the two-qubit fidelity as over 0.9, not 0.91.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because of the stochastic nature of the protocol, they cannot ensure the approximation converges asymptotically to the eigenvectors with the number of iterations.
quotes: Due to the stochastic nature of this protocol, we cannot ensure that the approximation converges asymptotically with the number of iteration to the eigenvectors.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit of its protocol.

assertions.value: The authors report that VQE, in general, gets better fidelities in the single-qubit case but uses more than 100 times the resources of their algorithm.
quotes: VQE, in general, get better fidelities in the single-qubit case but use more than 100 times the number of resources than our algorithm
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical comparison from one study.

papers.title_in_file: Scalable quantum neural networks by few quantum resources
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Section 5 Conclusions; model derivation and Proposition 6 not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A theoretical construction of a quantum model from repeated swap tests that is equivalent to a two-layer feedforward neural network.

assertions.value: The authors state that the model is equivalent to a two-layer feedforward neural network that can be realized by combining small quantum modules.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, p.1; Proposition 6 gives the equivalence up to an error
quotes: The model turns out to be equivalent to a two-layer feedforward neural network which can be realized combining small quantum modules.
assertions.certainty_reason: Proposition 6 (equivalence up to an error); the abstract states it without the error term.
assertions.reader_inference: The equivalence is approximate, so the abstract wording is looser than the proposition.

assertions.value: The authors state they assume the availability of specific-purpose quantum hardware, called a module, that can implement the swap test.
quotes: we assume the availability of a specific-purpose quantum hardware, that we call module, capable of implementing the swap test
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its assumption, Section 5, p.13.

assertions.value: The authors state that the empirical evaluation of the model is not addressed in the paper and only a theoretical construction is provided.
quotes: The empirical evaluation of the proposed model is not addressed in the present paper where only a theoretical construction is provided.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope, Section 5, p.13.

papers.title_in_file: Feature Importance and Explainability in Quantum Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, results discussion, Section IX Conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A small study that applies feature importance and explainability methods to classical and hybrid quantum classifiers on the Iris dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that feature importance and explainability methods can be applied to QML models and are potential candidates as tools in explainable quantum machine learning.
quotes: This article displays that these methods can indeed be applied to QML models, and so are potential candidates as tools in the unexplored field of explainable quantum machine learning, or XQAI.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result from one small study.

assertions.value: The authors state they have not necessarily seen a reliable example of quantum advantage in their QML models, probably due to the small scale of the data.
quotes: we haven't necessarily seen a reliable example of the quantum advantage in our QML models, probably due to the small scale of the data
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical finding from one small study; the cause is the authors' guess.

assertions.value: The authors state that the lack of models trained on an actual quantum computer was one of the greatest limitations of the article, because a simulator was used.
quotes: The lack of models trained on an actual quantum computer was one of the greatest limitations of this article, as a simulator was used
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its limit.

assertions.value: The authors state they use the Iris dataset to compare classical SVM and Random Forests with hybrid quantum counterparts, the Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) and Quantum Support Vector Classifier (QSVC).
quotes: Utilizing the widely recognized Iris dataset, classical ML algorithms
the Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) and Quantum Support Vector Classifier (QSVC)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup, Abstract.
